method: code inspection; no test exercises these properties

findings.claim: Only DesktopAgent, in the signed-in user's session, displays notifications; no service or server process renders them
evidence: Toast APIs (Microsoft.Toolkit.Uwp.Notifications) are referenced only in src/HashRelay.Agent: AgentContext.cs, OneClick.cs, Program.cs, Toasts.cs
src/HashRelay.Agent/HashRelay.Agent.csproj: OutputType WinExe (a tray app, not a Windows service)
build.ps1:57 publishes HashRelay.Server for linux-x64; the server has no toast code

findings.claim: On Windows, notifications go through the Windows App SDK AppNotificationManager
evidence: src/HashRelay.Agent/HashRelay.Agent.csproj:25 references Microsoft.Toolkit.Uwp.Notifications; the agent uses ToastNotificationManagerCompat (AgentContext.cs:77)
findings.note: Both libraries deliver to the Windows notification center from the user session, so the intent of the decision holds. The library named in the decision text is wrong; it was carried over from docs/adr/0001-windows-first.md without checking the code.

findings.claim: The Windows agent ships as a self-contained x64 build
evidence: HashRelay.Agent.csproj: SelfContained is true whenever a RuntimeIdentifier is set

findings.claim: Per-user Inno Setup installer that needs no admin rights

limits: Inspection of source and build scripts at the commit above. It does not run the installer, does not observe toasts on a machine, and does not prove that no future process renders notifications.
